static_traits.name: Chen Bowen
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, together with two pet dogs
static_traits.social_status: Social support is weak, lacking someone to confide in; interaction with colleagues tends to be strained due to stress
static_traits.medical_history: Denies major physical illness; has not previously received psychotherapy; no history of similar problems
static_traits.language_features: Clear and organized expression; negative tone, often uses all-or-nothing expressions; able to identify and state inner feelings; cooperation acceptable, willing to try to change

basic_info.main_problem: After being late to work for the first time last month, I feel my perfect attendance record is ruined, leading to persistent high anxiety and stress; I believe there is no point trying to be on time anymore, my motivation has dropped, and I worry about being late again, affecting my work performance and daily routine.
basic_info.core_demands: Seeks help because of this matter's impact on job satisfaction and mental health, and hopes to make a change.

core_beliefs: Only perfection counts as success / has value

special_situations.event: Last month, being late for work for the first time, causing perfect attendance to be broken
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am late once, it equals failure; no longer being perfect means I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly pressures themselves and thinks about the matter repeatedly, trying to maintain control by denying feelings or self-comforting with 'this one mistake does not define me', but with poor effect
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have ruined everything; since it is no longer perfect, no amount of effort has meaning

special_situations.event: Thinks about possibly being late again in the future (especially when approaching work or in daily arrangements)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am late one more time, it will prove I cannot do anything right
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent worry and rumination, excessive focus on time, sacrificing self-care in an attempt to avoid risk
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I am late again, I am finished; it proves I really am incapable

special_situations.event: Having arrived on time that day, but still recalling that one time being late
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive results that meet the standard do not count and cannot offset that one mistake
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring current achievements and relief cues, continuing to focus on potential negative outcomes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Being on time today is useless; I may still be late tomorrow

special_situations.event: Recalling the fact that 'perfect attendance was ruined'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A single mistake will reduce all past effort to nothing, and it cannot be remedied
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces anxiety with a giving-up / passive attitude (such as 'I no longer care about punctuality')
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All effort has been wasted; persisting has no meaning anymore

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a reliable, punctual, and self-disciplined person
core_conflict.fear: Fears that once imperfect, they will be negated and seen as incompetent, thereby losing a sense of self-worth
defense_goal: Maintains order and a sense of control through all-or-nothing high standards
Avoids the anxiety and shame of failing again by declaring 'I no longer care about punctuality'

object_relations.self_representation: Once I make a mistake, I will be proven to be someone who 'cannot do anything right'
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge (such as work standards / others' evaluations) that may negate the self at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about 'perfect attendance has been ruined', or when invited to view the problem in shades of gray rather than black and white
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes one mistake equals total failure, using 'since it is not perfect, there is no need to try anymore' to find reasons for giving up
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone carries self-justification and assertion, uses words such as 'anyway / since / why bother', and quickly negates the necessity of further exploration.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Interacting with colleagues under high pressure and intense anxiety about being late
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Converts tension about own mistakes and high standards into irritability and impatience toward the outside
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone is abrupt and stiff, reducing explanation and empathy, answering back or ending conversations with short sentences.

manifestations: A single instance of being late is experienced as 'making all effort meaningless'
Even when punctual that day, it is hard to experience a sense of achievement; small victories are overshadowed by long-term anxiety
Life is described as a 'repetitive stress cycle', making it hard to obtain a sense of meaning from daily life
outcomes: Decreased job satisfaction and strained interpersonal relationships

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treats 'perfect attendance' as an absolute standard that must be achieved; one deviation equals failure
Defining self-worth by external rules, difficulty absorbing and adjusting to exceptional cases

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Using absolutist self-negation (such as 'I cannot do anything well')
In counseling, acknowledges 'knowing it is irrational but just feeling that way', holds a cautious attitude toward change, and persistently blames themselves

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Lacks actions of seeking others' support, internalizing stress and anxiety and depleting the self
Sacrificing self-care and daily recovery due to anxiety

exception_events.target_problem: When approaching work time or thinking of possibly being late, the client usually falls into persistent anxiety and self-negation, leading to work distraction and reduced efficiency.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On some days when he arrived on time, he did not continue to give up or negate himself as usual, but completed arriving at work on time and maintained basic work tasks; although the anxiety was present, it was more bearable.
exception_events.reason: Clues: despite the anxiety, still went out according to the established routine and followed the schedule, enabling punctuality and basic performance to be maintained this time.

positive_force: Places high value on punctuality and professional ethics; has internal standards
Able to identify and express emotional distress, and proactively seeks counseling help
Open attitude toward change, willing to try new cognitive and behavioral strategies
Still able to arrive on time for many days, showing preserved executive function and self-discipline
The pet provides some emotional support and companionship
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking and perfectionist standards lead to total negation after frustration
Catastrophizing and future-predicting aggravate persistent anxiety
Disqualifying positive evidence and mental filtering make it hard to retain a sense of achievement
Continuous rumination and self-blame harm self-care and recovery
Weak social support system, lacking emotional support and reality correction

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive worry about being late and persistent rumination (anxiety)
antecedent: 临近上班或在上班途中
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white standards for perfect attendance and catastrophizing cognition about being late again
target_behavior.function: Attempts to gain a sense of control through high vigilance and rumination, avoiding uncertainty and failure
target_behavior.consequence: Distracted at work, efficiency declines, self-care and daily routine are impaired, and anxiety is maintained and worsens

target_behavior.behavior: Irritable toward colleagues, speaking briefly and impatiently
antecedent: Interacting with colleagues while under high pressure or in a highly anxious state
Small errors occur at work or time is tight
target_behavior.core_reason: Transferring anxiety about one's own mistakes and harsh standards to a safer target
target_behavior.consequence: Strained relationships with colleagues, further weakening social support, forming a negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Giving up on trying to be on time (passive avoidance and decreased motivation)
antecedent: When facing the need to invest extra effort to ensure punctuality
target_behavior.core_reason: All-or-nothing beliefs lead to negating the value of sustained effort once imperfect
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the shame and anxiety brought by failing again
target_behavior.consequence: Increasing the risk of being late again, reinforcing self-negation and sense of meaninglessness
